# Assignment before a panicking store

This is the original generated subject from baseline seed 4393 (`case_00151`)
in the September 17 audit's campaign, generated by grossmith `e68867d`.
The source is preserved exactly; it does not depend on replaying a historical
generator tape. The current `-check` driver observes its 19 return values.

In `v11, v12[v0] = h1(...)`, the first assignment must set `v11` to the empty
string before the second store panics on an out-of-range index. The recovery
wrapper returns that partial state, with panic-site slot 3. On Go 1.26.5,
result index 11 is `""` and index 18 is integer 3.

GoLean `3d2158224d06b6d7118c4f2af7a4c125c88768be` instead returned `"gros"` at
index 11. GoLean `3bb8f4fc9cd7dab16571787140731b6d4c1f9d0e` matches gc. This
was an inherited clone divergence, not a regression from the grossmith
improvement branch.

Run from the repository root with a current GoLean checkout:

```sh
GOLEAN_CHECKOUT=/path/to/golean go test ./golean -run '^TestGoLeanAssignmentBeforePanic$' -count=1
go run ./cmd/gengo -check golean/testdata/assignment-before-panic/subject.go -clone golean:/path/to/golean -out checked-assignment
go run ./cmd/gengo -verify checked-assignment
```

The GoLean test is opt-in because the bundled development checkout can predate
the clone fix. The nightly runs it against the checkout it just built.
